source.title: Have Faith in Faithfulness: Going Beyond Circuit Overlap When Finding Model Mechanisms
source.authors: Michael Hanna; S. Pezzelle; Yonatan Belinkov

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates IOI circuit faithfulness using corrupted-run activations on GPT-2 small, and also compares circuit-finding methods and metrics. Its circuits are automatically selected edge circuits, not the original 26-head circuit.
record.gate_note: The paper tests faithfulness on IOI, compares discovered circuits with the manually identified circuit, and reports cross-task circuit faithfulness. It does not test backup-head takeover, the stated roles of the seven head classes under patching, or IOI behavior across name orders, templates, or numbers of names. Results cited from the original IOI study are not recorded as this paper's results. Non-IOI task results and values used only to choose settings are omitted.
record.test_reason: It uses automated circuit-finding (EAP, EAP-IG, activation-patching scores) on GPT-2 small IOI and compares the results with the manual IOI circuit through node/edge precision-recall and an overlap-selected EAP circuit. That bears on V4, whether other methods recover the same circuit. It never evaluates the original 26-head circuit itself, so V1 and V5 are not tested directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that EAP-IG circuits are as faithful as or more faithful than EAP's. Activation-patching circuits still sometimes beat both, notably on IOI with logit diff. High overlap with manual circuits does not imply faithfulness, so faithfulness should be measured directly, including across tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses corrupted-input activation patching to measure circuit faithfulness, but selects edge circuits with EAP, EAP-IG, or activation-patching scores rather than directly testing the original 26-head circuit. Faithfulness is reported as normalized task performance; the paper also compares logit-difference and KL scoring.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI faithfulness differed by circuit-finding method and scoring metric; the IOI method gap was reported for logit difference but not KL divergence. Faithfulness also varied with EAP-IG step count. The study does not vary the IOI prompt distribution or the faithfulness ablation type.

fits_no_version.finding: EAP-IG with 2 steps mimics EAP's IOI faithfulness spike, while more than 2 steps gives similar, high faithfulness. This concerns the circuit-finder's hyperparameter.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-based edge attribution needs only a few integration steps to find faithful circuits.

fits_no_version.finding: Moderate circuit overlap does not predict cross-task faithfulness. Node and edge IoU correlate with faithfulness (r=0.86 and 0.83) but fail at moderate overlap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuit overlap is not a substitute for measuring faithfulness.

record.problems: The central IOI comparisons are reported mainly as qualitative descriptions of curves rather than exact values. Larger-model evaluations use only 100 examples per task and omit activation-patching circuits due to computational constraints. Cross-task IOI values appear in a figure without IOI-specific numerical descriptions in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Non-IOI task faithfulness results and their circuit comparisons are omitted. Larger-model GPT-2 XL and Pythia-2.8B curves are not included because they report faithfulness of newly found circuits, not whether the same head classes and roles carry IOI. Other method-variant IOI curves in Appendix D are not separately extracted because the text gives no IOI-specific numeric outcome for each variant.

untested.parts: The original 26-head circuit's faithfulness, completeness, minimality and head-class roles are never evaluated; only automated circuits are.
Backup name-mover takeover is not tested.

Same head classes in other models, sizes or checkpoints are not tested. The GPT-2 XL and Pythia-2.8B runs report only faithfulness of newly found circuits. IOI-specific cross-task values are not stated in the text.
The study does not vary the ablation type, evaluation metric or prompt distribution when evaluating the IOI circuit, and the manual circuit is not evaluated.
Name orders, templates and more names are not tested.

missing.what: Node and edge IoU between the IOI circuit and the other task circuits. All pairs have at least 0.25 node IoU, and edge IoU is often 0.05–0.15. This bears on reuse of IOI components for other tasks.
IOI faithfulness of EAP-IG variants (Marks et al., Miller et al., Clean-Corrupted baseline) versus activation patching. Miller's variant does comparatively well on IOI.

record.verdict_notes: The study's main object is the circuit-finding method, not the Wang et al. circuit. The record's V1 and V5 links are dropped because the manual circuit is never evaluated, and the logit-diff versus KL variation is a finder loss, not an evaluation choice. Cross-task IOI values exist only in figures. The paper also states without testing that mean ablation would likely give similar results to patching.

versions.untested_parts: The exact original 26-head circuit, its seven classes and roles, completeness, minimality, and the original circuit's own faithfulness are not directly tested. The IOI faithfulness results concern circuits selected by the paper's methods; one result concerns an EAP circuit selected for at least 90% node overlap with the manual circuit.
Whether backup heads take over when main name-mover heads are ablated is not tested.

The paper tests cross-task faithfulness of the selected IOI circuit, but does not establish that the same head classes and roles carry IOI in other models, sizes, or checkpoints. It also does not identify particular IOI components as reused for other tasks.

Circuit-finding methods and some scoring metrics are compared, but alternative faithfulness ablation types are not evaluated. The paper does not establish that all methods recover essentially the same circuit.
The paper tests sensitivity to circuit-finding method, scoring metric, and IG step count. It does not compare faithfulness ablation types or prompt distributions.
Name orders, alternative templates, and prompts with more names are not compared.
